subject.title: Provider key pools + bucket-aware cooldown/backoff on 429 (Gemini projects) to prevent retry storms

question: Should OpenClaw add a native quota-bucket contract for Gemini project/account-scoped provider failures, and should that live in core auth/failover or a provider/plugin-owned seam?
rationale: The choice affects public config or metadata shape, persisted cooldown state, fallback semantics, docs/status output, and core-versus-provider ownership, so automation cannot safely choose the product/API boundary.

options.title: Add generic quota buckets
options.body: Introduce additive provider/auth bucket metadata and bucket-level cooldown semantics while keeping today's flat key/profile rotation as the default.

options.title: Fold into provider-pool routing
options.body: Make the broader provider-profile routing tracker own Gemini project/account quota buckets before implementing this slice.

options.title: Keep outside core
options.body: Require provider plugins or sidecars to handle project-aware suppression if maintainers decide current seams are sufficient.

recommendation.title: Add generic quota buckets
recommendation.body: Introduce additive provider/auth bucket metadata and bucket-level cooldown semantics while keeping today's flat key/profile rotation as the default.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest feature-history signal for the existing generic key-rotation surface and broader provider/auth product boundary.
